legend.target_workload: the workload nominated before timing; its whole-model win must repeat before installation
legend.timing_case: the captured input case behind this hypothesis's local kernel timings
legend.timing_workload: the workload behind a region's recorded shipped-kernel speedup
legend.model_ratios: per-workload products of incremental model ratios; diagnostic estimates, not final measurements
legend.p: share of one step this region costs, all copies together, per workload
legend.T_orig_ms: library time for all copies, per workload, from pricing
legend.T_rep_ms: library time for one copy, per workload, from pricing
legend.roofline_ms: estimated ideal cost of one copy from boundary traffic and arithmetic
legend.s_max: optimistic headroom estimate: library time divided by estimated ideal cost
legend.bound: estimated limiting resource: memory, known compute, or launch; custom arithmetic may be unknown
legend.s: speedup shipped: the library's time over the shipped kernel's, both from the kernel's own ship clock
legend.region_ms: the kernel's time for one pass of one copy, from the ship clock
legend.library_ms: the library's time for the same pass, measured beside it
legend.win_ms: library_ms minus region_ms; positive means the kernel is faster
legend.sigma_ms: uncertainty of win_ms; a ship needs a win past three of these
legend.stranded: regions dropped before the search, grouped by reason
legend.steps_per_sample: dependent model steps in one timed sample of the step clock; more than one when a step is too short to bring the GPU clock up on its own
legend.min_win_ms: the least a region win had to save per step on this workload: 1% of the step, at most constants.min_win_ms; the three-sigma rule decides the rest
legend.speedup_vs_plain: under the compiled baseline: the finished model against plain eager MLX, paired in one window at the end of the job; compile's own gain is included, since the model runs compiled
legend.speedup_vs_compiled: under the plain baseline: the finished model (eager plus its kernels) against the untouched model under mx.compile, measured the same way; under 1 means compile alone is faster
legend.plain_win_confirmed: whether that comparison resolved a win past three sigma (compiled_win_confirmed likewise)
legend.plain_loss_confirmed: whether it resolved a loss (compiled_loss_confirmed likewise)
legend.measured_compute_gflops: the plain-matmul rate per dtype clocked in the region's own pricing window; the compute term of its estimated limit divides the region's flops by it
legend.close_rule: why a region's search ended: its budget or the job's is spent, the operator asked to finish, or no discernible headroom (launch-bound, head unmoved by the last two attempts, the last three kernels each within one sigma of the launch floor clocked beside them)
legend.constants.openers_per_region: how many attempts a region's widening round holds at most, each an opener written against the scaffold from a different agent-generated direction; limited by the remaining attempt budget
legend.delivery: how a kernel installs at the region's scope, per workload: direct, graph (the scope compiled with the cut inserted) or replay
legend.library_arm: what the region's clocks ran the library as, per workload: plain ops, or one compiled graph where graph delivery compiles the scope
legend.baseline.clocks_ms.compiled: under library inference: the model with its outermost compilable scopes compiled and empty, the baseline unless the manifest asks for plain
legend.final.delivery: under a plain baseline: the untouched model against the installed scopes compiled with no kernel, and that against the patched model

hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Four library launches become one: each thread reads a and b once, forms s=a+b, applies MLX's exact Sigmoid formula (y=1/(1+exp(-|s|)), flip for negative) and writes s*y. The two identical adds collapse into one register value, saving three launches and all intermediate memory traffic; bit-exactness relies on reproducing the library's sigmoid expression.
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.hypothesis: h1 used metal::exp and a plain 1.0f/x; if the harness pins fast-math on, the division becomes an approximate reciprocal and exp may be the fast variant, while MLX builds its library with precise math. Replace them with metal::precise::exp and metal::precise::divide so the sigmoid rounds exactly as the library kernel does; everything else unchanged.
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.hypothesis: Use the plain sigmoid form s*(1/(1+exp(-s))) without the abs/branch and fast division, dropping the select; a changing edit within tolerance that tests whether the shorter ALU path matters, and serves as a fallback if the exact formula in h1-h3 fails the preserving check.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Each thread handles four contiguous elements through float4 loads/stores using the plain sigmoid form, cutting the launch to 1024 threads (4 threadgroups of 256) and issuing wider memory transactions; tests whether fewer, wider threads shorten this launch-bound dispatch compared with h4's one-thread-per-element form. Declared changing because the exact bit-match gate failed for both h1 variants.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Launch a single threadgroup of 256 threads looping over the array with a grid stride (16 elements per thread) using the plain sigmoid; avoids scheduling multiple threadgroups across cores for a 16 KB problem, testing whether one-core residency beats h4's 16 threadgroups and h2's 4. Differs from h2 in launch shape rather than data width.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compute s*sigmoid(s) as s*0.5f*(1+tanh(0.5f*s)): a single transcendental with no division, cutting the per-element ALU path; at the launch floor this mostly tests whether shader length shifts the ~4.2us result at all, and a correct kernel is a usable parent.
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: outliers; regime; nonfinite_pattern; 6 elements break the non-finite pattern

hypotheses.kind: single 64-thread threadgroup streaming float4 with exp sigmoid
hypotheses.hypothesis: 64 threads in one threadgroup, each looping over float4 chunks with stride 64 (16 float4 per thread at 4096), using the direct 1/(1+exp(-s)) form that passed in h4/h2 instead of tanh (which produced NaN for large-magnitude inputs); tests whether a minimal dispatch footprint trims the launch-floor time versus h3's 256-thread loop.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 512 threads as two threadgroups of 256, each thread handling two float4 chunks; splits the middle between h2 (4 threadgroups) and h3 (1), testing whether a 2-core split moves the launch-floor result.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: many small threadgroups across all cores
hypotheses.hypothesis: Prior attempts used 1-16 threadgroups of 256; all sat at the ~4us launch floor. Launch 1024 float4 threads as 32 threadgroups of 32 threads so the dispatcher can place work on every one of the 10 cores at once; tests whether threadgroup count (rather than thread count or data width) is what limits the tiny stream, using the exp-based sigmoid that passes tolerance.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 2048 float2 threads in 32 threadgroups of 64: halves per-thread work versus float4 while keeping many groups; a middle point between h8 and h4 to see if any launch geometry moves off the floor.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: one dispatch of 4096 threads: each thread loads in0[i], in1[i], computes s=in0+in1 once, writes s to out0 and 1/(1+exp(-s)) to out1; this collapses the library's separate add/add/sigmoid launches into a single launch, which is the lever since the region is launch-bound (~4us per launch); the exp form is chosen because tanh-form sigmoid produced NaNs on outliers in the sibling region
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1024 threads each handle a float4 (reinterpret buffers as float4), computing the sum vector once and both outputs; fewer threads and 16-byte transactions could shave the per-thread overhead relative to h1 while keeping the single dispatch; differs from h1 in data width and thread count
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.hypothesis: h2 reproduced MLX's abs-then-select sigmoid but still missed bit-exactness on out1, so the residual difference is likely the transcendental/division variant: MLX's library is built with fast-math, so its exp and 1/(1+e) lower to the fast exp and reciprocal paths; using metal::fast::exp and metal::fast::divide explicitly should reproduce those bits regardless of the pinned compile mode
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.hypothesis: both the default and explicit fast exp/divide missed bit-exactness; MLX's own metallib is compiled with -fno-fast-math, so its Sigmoid (y=1/(1+exp(-|x|)), x<0?1-y:y) uses the precise exp and IEEE division; using metal::precise::exp and metal::precise::divide should reproduce the library bits regardless of the harness-pinned mode
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: stored_ref; exact; output must match the original bit-for-bit

hypotheses.kind: tolerance-tagged fused, two float4 per thread across 2 threadgroups
hypotheses.hypothesis: three preserving attempts (textbook, abs-select, fast, precise) all missed bit-exactness on out1 while out0 passed, so the library sigmoid bits are not reproducible from a custom body; declare the kernel changing so out1 is judged by tolerance, and fuse add+sigmoid into one dispatch of 512 threads each handling two float4 (in the two halves of the array) so the 32 KB of output is streamed by 2 threadgroups; differs from h1/h2 by the tolerance tag and by two vectors per thread; a correct result here gives a timed parent for launch-geometry experiments
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: same tolerance-tagged fused math but one element per thread across 16 threadgroups of 256, to test whether spreading groups over all 10 cores beats the 2-group float4 layout at this launch-bound size
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: the previous fused kernels named in0_shape, which makes the harness bind an extra shape buffer per dispatch; at this launch-bound size (library ~4.6us, ours ~5.1us) the argument encoding may be the residual overhead. Specialize to the captured length via a fallback_predicate, read no shape buffers, and keep one element per thread across 16 groups; expected effect is a slightly cheaper dispatch
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: one threadgroup of 1024 threads each handling a float4 covers 4096 elements in one group; tests whether a single-group dispatch schedules faster than multi-group at this size, differing from h3 (2 groups of 512 x2 float4) and h4 (16 groups scalar)
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: compute sigmoid as 0.5*(1+tanh(0.5*s)), which lowers to a single tanh op rather than exp plus division; tolerance-tagged, tests whether shorter shader latency shows up at this size
hypotheses.summary: failed at smoke: outliers; regime; nonfinite_pattern; 6 elements break the non-finite pattern

hypotheses.kind: fix: guard tanh sigmoid against overflow
hypotheses.hypothesis: h7's tanh identity broke the non-finite pattern on 6 outlier elements, most likely because the fast tanh lowering overflows to inf/inf=NaN for very large |s| where the original sigmoid saturates to 0 or 1; guard with a saturation select for |s| > 20 (NaN falls through to tanh and stays NaN) so the single-tanh path keeps its shorter latency while matching the original's finite pattern
